transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~57m
Attendees: Ian Murphy (Redwood AE), Sara Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Trident ML), Carlos Ruiz (Trident Platform), Lena O'Neill (Trident Head of ML)
Shared links: Benchmark spreadsheet (raw): https://redwood.app/sheets/bench-trident-quant ; Security deck (excerpt): https://redwood.app/docs/sec-trident

[00:00] Ian Murphy: ok hi everyone, thanks for joining, um this is our weekly checkpoint for the quant pilot, quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya Patel: Maya here, sorry running a bit late on my side,
[00:11] Carlos Ruiz: Carlos on platform, laptop dying but i'm good,
[00:15] Lena O'Neill: Lena here,
[00:18] Sara Chen: Sara from Redwood, hey all.

[00:22] Ian Murphy: Great. Quick agenda — perf delta recap, quality snapshots, tuning options we tried this week, and then next steps. Sara you want to start with the numbers?
[00:31] Sara Chen: Yeah sure. So we re-ran the baseline FP16 runs and the INT8/FP8 variants against the 128-token render set you sent. Baseline FP16 median p95 end-to-end latency for that slice was about 340ms per request with our current batching config at batch size 8 and 32 concurrent streams. INT8 reduced median p95 to ~260ms, FP8 to ~235ms. These are end-to-end numbers including network, scheduling and KV cash lookup overheads — sorry KV cache, autocorrect.
[01:05] Maya Patel: Sorry can you repeat that p95 delta? I want to make sure i'm capturing it.
[01:09] Sara Chen: FP16 340ms, INT8 260ms, FP8 235ms. So roughly 22-30% drop for INT8 and another ~10% improvement with FP8 vs INT8 on that workload.
[01:21] Carlos Ruiz: That's pretty significant. What about token throughput?
[01:24] Sara Chen: Good question. Tokens/sec increased from ~85 t/s (FP16) to ~110 t/s (INT8) and ~125 t/s (FP8) on the same instance class. But these numbers are sensitive to sequence length and KV-cache hit-rate.
[01:36] Lena O'Neill: And quality? we talked about that last week — did the eval harness show regressions?
[01:40] Sara Chen: We ran your annotated eval set — roughly 2,400 examples. The overall quality score we use in the harness (blend of exact-match for code tasks and semantic score for QA) dropped by 1.4% on INT8 and 0.9% on FP8 compared to FP16 baseline. That's average; some prompt families had larger deltas, others were negligible.
[01:56] Maya Patel: Hmm okay. We care about the few percent drift but only if it impacts production results on key prompts — we have SLA on top answers.
[02:04] Ian Murphy: Right — this is where the prompt-level triage helps. Maya, you mentioned in the ticket you'd highlight top failing prompts? Have you had a chance?
[02:11] Maya Patel: I started, uploaded 40 cases to the sheet, about 12 look clearly worse on int eight — more hallucinations and sometimes truncated completions. I'll share the full 200 sample set by monday.
[02:23] Carlos Ruiz: Do we have an idea which layers are causing biggest drop? any outlier dims?
[02:27] Sara Chen: We did a per-layer error heatmap. Most of the degradation clusters around a handful of MLP layers — apparent sensitivity in outlier activations. We think per-channel quant + larger group size helps; we tested symmetric per-tensor INT8 which was fastest but highest regressions. FP8 config uses block quantization and keeps some outlier ranges in FP16 — that's why FP8 had smaller quality impact.
[02:52] Lena O'Neill: Can we do hybrid? route critical traffic to FP16 and bulk to INT8?
[02:57] Ian Murphy: Yes that's one of the routing fallback options we discussed — policy-based routing by route/endpoint or even token-length. You can tag 'safety-critical' prompts to use FP16. That does increase cost for those invocations but keeps SLA.
[03:09] Carlos Ruiz: We also need to think about model drift and eval cadence — if we deploy int8, do we plan automatic rollbacks?
[03:15] Sara Chen: Redwood has automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to your eval watchlist. We can set thresholds — if average quality drops >1% on the watch prompts for two consecutive hours we automatically shift traffic back to FP16 and open an alert.
[03:26] Maya Patel: Good. On infra side, we had one stall last night during the INT8 run — looked like an IO stall, not GPU bound. Sara, you mentioned NVMe reads in the logs?
[03:35] Sara Chen: Right — in the 02:14 run we saw a couple of 100-200ms spikes correlated with checkpoint prefetch and small file reads; our next sweep will pin the model fully in memory and increase prefetch window. Also prepping a run with larger batch size 16 to see throughput/latency tradeoffs — that will likely change the optimal batch for INT8 vs FP8.
[03:56] Carlos Ruiz: For on-prem test, we need the kernel timestamps and the exact container image tag. Can you provide that?
[04:01] Sara Chen: Yes, i'll include the docker digest and the kernel trace flags in the artifact bundle.
[04:06] Ian Murphy: Quick pause — any blockers from security/compliance standpoint for on-prem? Lena?
[04:09] Lena O'Neill: We need SOC2 attestation and an HSM/KMS flow for our keys, also wants to ensure audit logs are forwarded to our SIEM. We reviewed your security deck; looks good but we need a short runbook for the on-prem smoke test describing KMS handshake and who has keys.
[04:24] Ian Murphy: We'll add that to the runbook. Sara, can you create a step-by-step for the on-prem smoke?
[04:28] Sara Chen: Yep, i'll create a runbook and add the KMS section and audit log config.
[04:31] Maya Patel: Also, small ask — can we get a trimmed binary for FP8 variant? infra prefers smaller image for air-gapped staging.
[04:37] Sara Chen: We have a minimal runtime build; i'll attach the build artifact link. Note: smaller build excludes debug symbols, so logs won't have line-level traces.
[04:45] Ian Murphy: Back to quality — Sara you said some prompt families had bigger regressions. Can you give 2-3 examples?
[04:50] Sara Chen: Sure — example one: long-form summarization prompts where the model relied on subtle copying patterns; int8 produced more paraphrase errors. Example two: code-completion sequences where tokenization shifts caused subtle off-by-one changes in bracket placement. Example three: a safety filter false negative on one prompt where the score slightly crossed threshold.
[05:10] Maya Patel: The code completion ones worry me — those are customer-facing. Could we try mixed precision: keep key attention weights in fp16, quantize rest?
[05:17] Sara Chen: Yes, mixed precision per-module is supported. It reduces some speed benefits but often recovers quality. That is one of the configs we'll exercise in the next sweep.
[05:26] Carlos Ruiz: For metrics we want: p50/p95 end-to-end, tokens/sec, failure rate on annotated prompts, and cost delta per 1M tokens. Can you include cost estimation?
[05:34] Ian Murphy: We'll include a cost calc row in the spreadsheet — it factors in batch size, instance SKU, and expected hit-rate for KV cache. Sara will update the sheet.
[05:40] Sara Chen: Noted. Also we added a per-request trace id so you can correlate a problematic output back to kernel timestamps in the raw logs.
[05:48] Lena O'Neill: Good. About SLA — if we go with dedicated reserved capacity, can we get lower variance on p95?
[05:55] Ian Murphy: Yes dedicated GPUS reduce noisy neighbors and give predictable throughput; Dedicated plus reserved commitment also unlocks higher priority scheduling and smaller p95 tails. We'll share an SLO projection for dedicated vs hosted.
[06:08] Maya Patel: Are there config knobs specifically for reducing hallucinations introduced by quant?
[06:12] Sara Chen: A few — higher precision for normalization layers, preserving first/last token logits in fp16, and token clipping thresholds. Also calibration with representative data (your 200 samples) often helps the quantizer pick better scales.
[06:29] Carlos Ruiz: timeline question — if we agree to int8+fp8 pilot next week, when can we expect a production-like pilot?
[06:35] Ian Murphy: If we get your sample prompts by monday and we run the full perf sweep w/ logs by tuesday/thursday, we can schedule an on-prem smoke the week of 2026-03-16. Production-like pilot could be staged in a canary roll week of 2026-03-23 depending on results.
[06:50] Maya Patel: Sounds reasonable. One more item: bias/regression checks — can Redwood run automated safety/regression evals against our watchlist?
[06:57] Sara Chen: Yes, we can run your watchlist as a gate. We also have an automated diff report that highlights changed tokens, scoring shifts and a short sample of failing outputs. We'll make that available in the sheet.
[07:12] Ian Murphy: ok let's summarize next steps briefly.
[07:15] Ian Murphy: Ian will run perf sweep with batch sizes 8/16/24, updated prefetch, and mixed-precision variants and post raw logs by 2026-03-09.
[07:24] Ian Murphy: Sara will prepare the on-prem runbook, attach docker digest and kernel trace flags, and upload trimmed FP8 build by 2026-03-06.
[07:33] Ian Murphy: Maya will provide the 200 sample prompts and annotate the high-priority watchlist by 2026-03-08.
[07:40] Carlos will coordinate infra for the on-prem smoke and confirm access method by 2026-03-10.
[07:46] Lena: i'll review the SOC2 artifact and confirm any gaps, will follow-up in the security thread.
[07:51] Sara Chen: i'll also update the benchmark spreadsheet with cost calc and p95_projection for dedicated vs hosted.
[07:58] Ian Murphy: Great. Any final questions or blockers?
[08:02] Maya Patel: No blockers, just need the logs and we'll triage the sample set as soon as we get them.
[08:07] Carlos Ruiz: Thanks all.
[08:09] Ian Murphy: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the ticket and i will email notes.
